thread.title: Alibaba Has as Much Bite as the Faangs - Barron's

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Alibaba Has as Much Bite as the Faangs - Barron's
text:
By Teresa Rivas May 7, 2018 10:33 a.m. ET Even with some big hiccups this year, tech has been outperforming, with the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) up 6.6% year-to-date. It's not just the Faang stocks-- Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL)--that are moving up; or maybe we need to add yet another 'A' to the group.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images American depositary receipts of Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) are up more than 12% since the start of the year, building on top of 2017's outperformance, and the company's "impressive" first-quarter results should see the shares move higher, argues Stifel's Scott Devitt, who reiterated a Buy rating on the shares Monday.
Devitt writes that sales came in well ahead of consensus estimates, and while Alibaba's margins were below his expectations, that's due to the company's investments in new retail, international growth, customer-acquisition and user experience (a process that echoes Amazon's own investments that weighed on profits, but have paid off well of late).
Devitt thinks that a similar process is taking place at Alibaba, and his bullish thesis is predicated on the fact that "areas of investment [are] widening the addressable market, supporting longer term growth, and strengthening the company’s position." He also raised his price target by $2, to $262.
As we've noted before, it wouldn't be the first time Amazon and Alibaba employed similar business strategies .
Alibaba is up 2.8% to $194.09 this morning. Faaang anyone?
